**[action]** Wrote one self-contained HTML file:
- **Layout/visual language:** white ground (`--paper`), thick black rules/borders, Jost sans (geometric, like the type Mondrian favoured), red/blue/yellow as the only accents, everything rectilinear — no curves, no diagonals. Sections are numbered 01/02/03 on a hard black grid.
- **Hero canvas:** Three.js r170 `OrthographicCamera` + `MeshBasicMaterial` planes recreating the described composition (large red square top-right, small blue square bottom-left, small yellow rectangle bottom-right, thick black dividing lines on white), with a barely-perceptible zoom "breath" disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Content sections:** The painting (title/painter/year/medium/collection/movement as a `<dl>`); The movement (De Stijl founded 1917 by van Doesburg & Mondrian; Neoplasticism principles as four blocks plus a colour key); Why it matters (asymmetric balance → reference for graphic design & architecture, with an accurate Large/Small/Small band); Read more CTA linking to the Wikipedia source URL from the fact sheet.
- Assumptions stated in-page: exact hex primaries, typography and motion were left open by the brief — chose Mondrian-appropriate defaults; the canvas art is labelled "an interpretation after the 1930 composition", not a reproduction, so nothing false is claimed about pixels of the real work.

**[result]** Verified live in the browser: page loads from `file://`, text content reads correctly end-to-end (all six facts present verbatim-consistent with FACTSHEET.md), `import('three@0.170.0')` resolves (`THREE r170`), WebGL context creates, `scrollWidth === clientWidth` = 1265 (no horizontal overflow), `.band` renders three equal columns with corrected Large/Small/Small labels, footer carries the source attribution. No second round needed beyond fixing the earlier mislabelled "2 squares" band. Browser tab closed.

**[next]** Deliverable ready: `<WORKSPACE>\landing\index.html`. Open it directly in any browser; needs network access only to fonts.googleapis.com and cdn.jsdelivr.net.
